searches.note: Twenty one searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's, and seven left unspent for the shared allowance. Two were restricted to a body's own domain and are read as primary through their summaries: boe.es, navarra.es and mapa.gob.es once (the Orden Foral 400/2007 of 4 October, its publication in the BOE of 24 January 2009, the pliego of the Pago de Arínzano and the estate at the foot of Montejurra by the Ega) and navarrawine.com once (the five subzones, the three damp northern ones, Valdizarbe the wettest on its own page, Baja Montaña the most Pyrenean, Ribera Alta warm and Ribera Baja the hottest). The rest went to the open web with the author's sources blocked where they would only have repeated themselves (chivite.com, bodegasochoa.com, artadi.com, arinzano.com, Vinissimus, Spanish Wine Lover, Bodeboca, Skurnik, Justerini and Brooks, Lebendige Weine, Thatcher's Wine, Harpers, Wikipedia, Enterwine and Noticias de Navarra by turns). The two shared searches are the research station of 1981 (Lupier, Ochoa's question) and the subzones (all five records). No WebFetch was tried. Every record was tested; no fact that rests on no source was kept.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word in the glass, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the bodies (the BOE, the Government of Navarra, the Ministry's pliego, the DO Navarra) and then to the press, guides and merchants for the second source of each house's date, with the author's sources blocked so that an independent account would show.

Where the sources corrected the record it was set right with its source (the deed of 1647, the oak of the Blanco, Legardeta and Arínzano, the sale of 2017, Traibuenas, the death of 1965, the parcels and heights of La Dama, the founding of Lupier, the monks of 1055, the seller of 2015, the oak of the Gran Vino, Valdizarbe, Artazuri); where a detail rested on one account or none it was cut (picking by hand and free run juice for the Blanco, Fermentado en barrica on the label, the thirty years of 2023, Oxoa, the grapes sold before 2008, tank and whole bunches at Lupier, the trials of Merlot, the share of new oak at Arínzano, the blends of La Casona and Hacienda).

Claims of a house's own dates, vineyards and methods stand, hedged as the house's account where they are its telling. Sources whose title or address names a living person, or that are a writer's own site, were met in the results but never cited (a wine blog named for its writer on Lupier, Wine with Seth on Arínzano); the fragment's sources were changed only where the record now rests on the refuter's, and every new source is listed per record under extraSources.

tested: 1647: the accounts read (INCABE, Proensa, a regional guide) describe a notarial loan of August 1647 for which members of the family pledged a bodega; some present it as the founding, one as the first record of vines. The year stands as the house's account; the deed now reads as the first record of the family's winery, not as proof of a member making wine.

1860 and 1985: the first export to Bordeaux in 1860 and Colección 125 launched in 1985 for 125 years of export, with the 125 Aniversario Gran Vino of 1981 at its origin, are borne out by INCABE and Proensa beside the house's milestones. Confirmed.

1993 and Denis Dubourdieu (1949 to 2016): Wine Enthusiast names him the creator of the Colección 125 Blanco in 1993, independent of the house; his dates are the OIV's and the house's. Confirmed. His late harvest Moscatel rests on the house alone and is now hedged as its account.

The site: a single north facing parcel of Finca Legardeta on clay loam at 480 metres is borne out by two merchants' sheets (Mesquevi, Vinopremier) beside the house. Confirmed. The Arínzano estate beside Legardeta is not borne out (Arínzano lies at Aberin, Legardeta at Villatuerta), so both are now simply in Tierra Estella.
The making: four listings give the Blanco ten, eleven or twelve months on its lees in French oak; picking by hand, a short maceration, free run juice and 225 litres rest on one sheet, and are cut.

Ownership: Perelada's own notice, Navarra Capital, OKDiario and Proensa give the purchase of the Chivite group by Grupo Peralada on 18 October 2017, the banks having held about four fifths of it since 2015. Legardeta is therefore the house's estate, not the family's, and the sale is told as history in the story.

The range: the Colección 125 Reserva is Tempranillo of Legardeta by most listings (one gives Syrah as well and is set aside); the Vendimia Tardía is Moscatel de Grano Menudo, botrytised and picked in several passes. Both others stand.
The label: Fermentado en barrica on older labels rests on no source read; Gran Vino Blanco is the wording of the house's page and of a merchant's listing, and takes its place.

The house rules: the family member who leads the house, the chairman kept on after 2017 and the buyer's president are living and are not named. No price or score: the merchants' prices met in the results are left out. Serve at 10 to 13 degrees Celsius agrees with the Codex's reference for a full white.

changed.was: The Chivite family dates itself to 1647: by its own account, a notarial deed of that year shows one of its members already making wine. In 1860 the house sent its first wine abroad, to Bordeaux, and in 1985 it marked 125 years of exporting with Colección 125, a range launched with a red of the 1981 vintage. In 1993 the Bordeaux oenologist Denis Dubourdieu (1949 to 2016) began working with the house, and the Colección 125 Blanco, a Chardonnay fermented in barrel, was his creation, as was a late harvest Moscatel. The Blanco came in time to be drawn from one parcel of Finca Legardeta, the family's estate by Villatuerta in Tierra Estella, beside the Arínzano estate that the family sold in 2015. In 2016 twenty eight vintages of the range were opened together at a vertical tasting in Madrid, the house's way of showing that its wines could age. The name is easily misread: the 125 counts years of export, not years of the house, whose records reach back more than three centuries. For a sommelier the Blanco is the bottle that shows Navarra Chardonnay, fermented and aged with care in French oak, can keep and gain in bottle.
changed.now: The Chivite family dates itself to 1647: by its own account, a notarial deed of that year is the first record of the family's winery. In 1860 the house sent its first wine abroad, to Bordeaux, and in 1985 it marked 125 years of exporting with Colección 125, a range launched with a red of the 1981 vintage. In 1993 the Bordeaux oenologist Denis Dubourdieu (1949 to 2016) began working with the house, and the Colección 125 Blanco, a Chardonnay fermented in barrel, was his creation; as the house tells it, so was a late harvest Moscatel. The Blanco came in time to be drawn from one parcel of Finca Legardeta, the house's estate by Villatuerta in Tierra Estella, where the family also held the Arínzano estate until it was sold in 2015. In 2016 the house opened twenty eight vintages of the range together at a vertical tasting in Madrid, its way of showing that the wines could age, and in 2017 Chivite passed to the Catalan Grupo Peralada. The 125 counts years of export, not years of the house. For a sommelier the Blanco is the bottle that shows Navarra Chardonnay, fermented and aged with care in French oak, can keep and gain in bottle.
changed.why: The deed of 1647 is a loan for which a bodega was pledged, so it is the first record of the family's winery; Arínzano is not beside Legardeta; Legardeta passed with the house to Grupo Peralada in 2017, so it is the house's estate and the sale is added as history; Dubourdieu's Moscatel rests on the house alone and is hedged; the line on the three centuries is cut for length, the trap keeping it.

tested: 1843 and six generations: De Bodega en Bodega gives the first stone in 1843 (with a forebear in 1837), the coverage of ADEFAN's family firm prize of 2024 gives six generations, and the Ruta del Vino and a distributor give 1845 for the founding. Founded stays empty; the story keeps 1843 as the timeline's first stone. Confirmed.

1965: De Bodega en Bodega gives the death of the head of the house in 1965 and his son, nineteen, taking charge, beside the house's timeline. Confirmed, but no source ties the man who died in 1965 to the planting of 1930, so the story no longer joins them, and came home is now took charge.

The making: the house's Aquí sheet (Bodegas Ochoa's own, hosted by CITI Navarra) and Bodeboca give the two late passes, in September as the grapes begin to raisin and in November when they are fully raisined, the very concentrated must fermenting to a sweet wine, Moscatel de Grano Menudo alone and more than ten years of life with tropical fruit when young. Confirmed. No source read speaks of noble rot, so the question's distractor stands.

The vineyard: the Aquí sheet says the Moscatel comes wholly from the finca El Bosque de Traibuenas; a merchant's listing names the wine Altos de Traibuenas. Planted to Moscatel alone is not what the sheet says, so the sites now read the vineyard at Traibuenas from which all its Moscatel comes.

The 1990s: Spanish Wine Lover says the family led the recovery of Moscatel de Grano Menudo and replanted after its head left the research station in 1992, and Verema lists a Moscatel of 1996; the 1990s stand. The thirty years marked in 2023 rest on one press article and are cut.

The others: Moscato de Ochoa, a lightly sparkling Moscatel of low alcohol, is on the house's page and three merchants. Confirmed. Oxoa appears on one merchant's listing only, its style not given, and is cut.

The house rules: the son who took charge in 1965 and his daughter, the cellar's oenologist, are living and are not named; the head of 1965 is described, his dates not found. Serve at 6 to 8 degrees Celsius agrees with the Codex's reference for a sweet white.

changed.was: Altos de Traibuenas, the family's vineyard planted to Moscatel de Grano Menudo alone, in the warm Ribera Alta subzone around Olite.
changed.now: The family's vineyard at Traibuenas, near Olite, from which, by the house's sheet, all its Moscatel de Grano Menudo comes, in the warm Ribera Alta subzone.
changed.why: The house's sheet says all its Moscatel comes from its finca at Traibuenas (El Bosque de Traibuenas there, Altos de Traibuenas on a listing); it does not say the vineyard is planted to Moscatel alone.

changed.was: The Ochoa family has grown vines at Olite, in the centre of Navarra, for six generations, and by its own timeline the first stone of its cellar was laid in 1843. In 1930 the head of the family planted a large vineyard on La Plana de Olite and, as the timeline tells it, released the house's first bottled reds aged in barrel. When he died in 1965, his son, nineteen years old, came home to run the bodega. The house also tells a legend of the grape it is known for: Moscatel de Grano Menudo, it says, came to Olite with a Navarrese king in the thirteenth century. By the late twentieth century the old Moscatel vines were close to being pulled up, and in the 1990s the family planted a new vineyard from old local vines and began to make a late harvest sweet wine from it; in 2023 the house marked thirty years of making Moscatel. The grapes of the Vendimia Tardía are picked in two passes, in September and in November, as they raisin on the vine. For a sommelier it is the bottle that teaches Navarra's second tradition beside its rosado: sweet white wine of the small berried Muscat.

tested: The founding: Vila Viniteca, Spectrum Wine and a regional guide give 2006, the year the couple bought the plots; the author's importers give 2008; the first commercial vintage of both wines is 2008 by several listings and The Wine Society's El Terroir 2009, the second. Founded is emptied for want of one year; 2006 for the plots and 2008 for the first vintage stand.

The plots: twenty seven micro plots of old Garnacha at San Martín de Unx are in Vila Viniteca, Falstaff, Vinello and others; the oldest planted in 1903 in two; heights of 400 to 750 metres in two and 400 to 800 in another. The author's 650 to 750 metres for La Dama's parcels and vines of about 120 years are replaced.

La Dama's parcels: two merchants give the 2018 from the five highest parcels, up to 800 metres; one merchant says a later vintage came from the lower part of the vineyard, with the upper part made apart. The record now says a selection of the parcels, the highest in its earlier vintages, and the wine question keyed on the highest parcels is replaced.

The making: fourteen months in French oak casks of 700, 500 and 300 litres in one sheet beside the author's two; fermented in tank, whole bunches and few new casks rest on one importer each and are cut.

The founders: a couple (Vinello and Global Stylus: one of them an agronomist and winemaker with years as technical director of viticulture for other bodegas, the other an economist); two merchants say they left their jobs to buy abandoned plots, in one shared wording, so that is not kept. That they sold their grapes before 2008 rests on no source read and is cut. Organic farming, uncertified, is in several accounts; biodynamic in some, so organically stands alone.

The research station: the Gran Enciclopedia de Navarra dates EVENA to 1981, at Olite, and its trial field held Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay among thirty five varieties; Merlot is not named there, so the story names the two and turns the trials into a sequence, not a cause.
The change of hands: merchants give the estate passing to a winemaker of Bierzo from the 2018 vintage, in 2022 and late in 2023; the story keeps the change without a year.

The house rules: the founding couple and the winemaker from Bierzo are living and are not named. No score: the merchants' points met in the results are left out. Serve at 15 to 17 degrees Celsius agrees with the Codex's reference for a medium red.

changed.why: 2006 for the plots in three accounts against 2008, the first vintage, in the importers'; a founding year nobody agrees on is left empty.

changed.was: Garnacha was once nearly the whole of Navarra's vineyard, much of it bound for rosado. After the regional research station opened at Olite in 1981, its trials led growers towards Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Chardonnay, and many old bush vines in the hills were abandoned. Domaines Lupier was built to keep some of them. Its founders, a couple who had worked in the wine trade, set out to rescue the old Garnacha of San Martín de Unx, in Baja Montaña. From 2006, by some importers' accounts, they began to buy small plots scattered over the hills, twenty seven of them in the end, some of the vines more than a century old, and for the first years they sold the grapes. In 2008 they bottled their first vintage. They farmed organically from the start and made two wines: El Terroir from most of the parcels, and La Dama from the highest. Later, by importers' accounts, the estate passed to a winemaker from Bierzo. For a sommelier La Dama is the bottle that shows Navarra Garnacha as a fresh, perfumed red of the hills, far from the deep pink rosado that made the region's name.
changed.now: Garnacha was long the main grape of Navarra, much of it bound for rosado. In the decades after the regional research station opened at Olite in 1981 and trialled Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay, many growers turned to grapes from abroad and to Tempranillo, and old bush vines in the hills were pulled up. Domaines Lupier was built to keep some of them. Its founders, a couple, one of them an agronomist and winemaker who had worked for other bodegas, set out to rescue the old Garnacha of San Martín de Unx, in Baja Montaña. From 2006 they bought small plots scattered over the hills, twenty seven of them in the end, the oldest planted in 1903, and in 2008 they bottled their first vintage. They farmed organically and made two wines: El Terroir from most of the parcels, and La Dama, drawn in its earlier vintages from the highest. Later the estate passed to a winemaker from Bierzo. For a sommelier La Dama is the bottle that shows Navarra Garnacha as a fresh, perfumed red of the hills, far from the deep pink rosado that made the region's name.
changed.why: Garnacha nearly the whole vineyard and the trials of Merlot are not borne out (the encyclopedia names Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay); the founders were an agronomist and winemaker and an economist, not a couple of the wine trade; the grapes sold before 2008 rest on no source; La Dama's highest parcels hold for its earlier vintages.

tested: The pago: the pliego of the Pago de Arínzano (the Ministry's file) cites the Orden Foral 400/2007 of 4 October of the Government of Navarra, and the BOE of 24 January 2009 carries the Orden ARM/4004/2008 that publishes it; the Government of Navarra's own page places the estate at Aberin, at the foot of Montejurra by the Ega. Confirmed. The first in northern Spain stays the estate's claim, hedged; every earlier pago read of was in Castilla-La Mancha.

The history: guides (Con Mucha Gula, Ungranvino) give 1055 as a royal grant of the land, not monks working vines, and a later gift to nearby monasteries in one; the tower is of the sixteenth century in most accounts, 1532 in one guide and the estate's page, the twelfth or fourteenth century in two others; phylloxera destroyed the vines more than a century before 1988 (Todowine). The monks of 1055 are cut; the tower keeps its hedge.

1988 and the winery: Todowine and the press of 2015 give the Chivite family's purchase and replanting of 1988; Arquitectura Viva bears out the winery designed as an arc enclosing the three old buildings; Navarra Capital dates its opening to 2002. The year 1997 is now hedged as the estate's.

2015: Vozpópuli, Navarra Capital and Pequeñas D.O's give the sale of Arínzano to the SPI group of Luxembourg in 2015, by Chivite, whose banks then held most of the group. The seller is now Chivite rather than the family.

The wine: Tempranillo alone by several listings (one gives a blend and seems to mix the range); fourteen to eighteen months in French oak barrels new and used in equal parts by the estate's brochure, fourteen months half new by a merchant's sheet, against the author's quarter new: the share is cut. Serve at 16 to 18 degrees Celsius agrees with a merchant's sheet and the Codex's reference.

The other pagos and the Rioja corner: Otazu and Prado de Irache are the region record's other two pagos, and the region record puts the Navarra towns of the DOCa Rioja in the south west of the province, around San Adrián and Andosilla; the explanation keeps the author's San Adrián, consistent with it, and is not changed.

The house rules: the architect, the buyer's owner, the former king who opened the winery by one account and the estate's winemaker are living and are not named. No price: the sale's figure met in the press is left out.

changed.was: By its own account Arínzano is documented from 1055, when monks worked vines in this valley of the Ega. From the sixteenth century it passed through noble families, who built a fortified tower, finished in 1532 as the estate tells it, and later a manor house, La Casona; from 1715 the land was given over to vines. Phylloxera later struck the vineyard, and in 1988 the Chivite family bought the estate and replanted it, with a Bordeaux oenologist advising. In 1997 a new winery was designed to enclose the three old buildings. In 2007 a foral order of the Government of Navarra, dated 4 October, recognised Arínzano as a Vino de Pago, a single estate with its own denomination, on Chivite's application; by the estate's account it was the first in northern Spain. In 2015 the Chivite family sold Arínzano to the SPI group, which made it the first estate of a new division of luxury wines. The Gran Vino Tinto is the estate's first red, a Tempranillo made in four lots and aged in French oak. For a sommelier it is the bottle that explains a pago: a wine of Navarra that is not a wine of DO Navarra.

tested: 1996 and the co-operative: International Wine Review and Ideavinos give 1996 for Artadi's coming to Artazu and an old, defunct village co-operative taken over; one merchant gives 2000 for the founding and the first release. Confirmed as the record tells it; founded keeps 1996.
Artadi of 1985 at Laguardia and its leaving the DOCa Rioja in 2015 are the library's p-artadi. Confirmed in the library; one listing's 1986 is set aside.

The white and the denomination: Tanino Wines and Decantalo give Santa Cruz de Artazu Blanco as Garnacha Blanca alone, DO Navarra, part of the house's project to recover the white Garnacha of Navarra, from plots at 450 to 600 metres on white clay and limestone. Confirmed, and the wines of Artazu still carry DO Navarra.

Artazuri: every listing read gives Artazuri as a dry rosado of Garnacha alone, from free run juice fermented in steel without oak, from the same heights and soils; a red appears once. The record's another varietal Garnacha is now Artazuri Rosado.

Valdizarbe: the DO's own pages put Tierra Estella, Valdizarbe and Baja Montaña together in the damp north, call Valdizarbe the wettest on its page and Baja Montaña the most Pyrenean; none calls Valdizarbe the coolest, so the label now says one of the three cooler, damper subzones of the north.
Santa Cruz a plot: no source read beyond the house's plot list (the author's) names it; it is hedged as the house's account.

The house rules: Artadi's founder is living and is not named. No score: the points met in the results are left out. Serve at 15 to 17 degrees Celsius agrees with the Codex's reference for a medium red.

livingNote: None of these is named in the fragment's prose; the read together agent adds those it judges living to people.json (Raúl Pérez is there already as the name of a house, which a house keeps). Long dead and named with dates: Denis Dubourdieu (1949 to 2016). Dead and described, never named, for want of dates: the members of the Chivite family in the deed of 1647 (Juan Chivite Frías, María Rubio and Joseph Chivite in one account), Claudio Chivite of the export of 1860, Adriano Ochoa, the head of the house who died in 1965, Valerio Ochoa of 1837, and the noble Lope de Eulate of Arínzano's sixteenth century.
swapNote: No swap was proposed by the author, and the refuter proposes none. The five are real houses of Navarra, each making the wine its record tells, which independent accounts bear out: Chivite, the old house of the province with its Colección 125; Ochoa of Olite, whose late harvest Moscatel teaches the region's sweet tradition; Domaines Lupier, the old Garnacha of Baja Montaña; Arínzano, the first of Navarra's three pagos; and Artazu, Artadi's Garnacha of Valdizarbe. The plan's pick for Arínzano names Arínzano Gran Vino and the record keeps Arínzano Gran Vino Tinto, which holds the plan's words.
planNotes: chivite: the note is answered: the house is sold as Chivite (J. Chivite Family Estates in some listings) and passed to Grupo Peralada in 2017, told as history; 1647, the naming of 1985 and the Blanco of 1993 are borne out; the label wording of recent vintages is Colección 125 Gran Vino Blanco on the house's page, and Colección 125 Chardonnay was not met. Denis Dubourdieu is named with his dates. The why stands.

ochoa: the note is answered: 1843 is the timeline's first stone and 1845 is given elsewhere, so founded stays empty; the label is Ochoa Moscatel Vendimia Tardía with Navarra; the Rosado de Lágrima was not searched and no blend is given. The why's unfortified stands on the house's naturally sweet and the region record.

lupier: the note is answered: La Dama and El Terroir are the two wines, La Dama the selection; the founding year is not settled (2006 or 2008), so founded is empty; the oldest vines were planted in 1903. The why stands.

arinzano: the note is answered: the pliego and the BOE bear out the Orden Foral of 4 October 2007; the first in northern Spain is the estate's claim and the region record's, hedged in the record, while the why states it flatly and may want a hedge; the label is Arínzano Gran Vino with the pago, Tempranillo alone in the vintages read; 1988 and 2015 are told as history from two sources each.
artazu: the note is answered: Artadi of Laguardia is the house behind it, 1996 is borne out by two independent accounts, and the label carries DO Navarra. The why stands.
